headline: High-risk filesystem/network interaction: xonsh can write and egress broadly while the other profile is unverified and may be exposed to prompt-injection-style content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel documented, but B reads and writes the filesystem and executes shell commands, so if A’s outputs are copied into files or stdin they can be treated as trusted content. A itself is source-available and unverified, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A’s output is copied into a file or stdin that B processes as instructions, injection is possible.
IF the operator bridges the agents through a shared workspace, B may parse attacker-controlled text as commands.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of A outputs into B command streams.
Require a human review step before B executes any text produced by A.
Use read-only handoff files for A outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad network egress and filesystem access, while A is unverified and source-available with no explicit data-handling limits. No sensitive data class is listed for A, so leakage is not proven, but any shared files or copied content could flow from A into B and then out over the network.
conditions: IF A receives sensitive files through a shared workspace, B can read them.
IF B is allowed to transmit its context or file contents, copied A material may leave the environment.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Restrict B’s network egress during joint runs.
Use separate OS users for A and B.
Review B’s outbound destinations before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; A’s profile does not expose write or coordination capabilities, so direct conflict is not symmetric. However, if both are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite artifacts produced by A. Uncertainty about A’s runtime surface escalates this above low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, B can overwrite A’s artifacts.
IF A is later extended with write access, concurrent edits may collide.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Make A outputs read-only before B consumes them.
Run only one writer at a time.
Snapshot shared files before B edits them.
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can execute shell commands and read files, so if it treats A’s output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into real actions. A is unverified and may emit misleading content; B’s tool-use pattern makes downstream execution plausible even without direct evidence of automation.
conditions: IF B consumes A output without validation, errors can propagate into shell actions.
IF A produces incorrect instructions, B may execute them as commands.
mitigations: Require explicit validation before B acts on A output.
Use a checklist for command execution.
Log and review all A-to-B handoffs.
Limit B to dry-run mode for joint tasks.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. A is source-available and unverified; B is open-source with no secrets handled. The pair therefore shows only a weak compliance gap, not a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into a shared workflow, compliance review is needed.
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees, neither profile documents them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in joint runs.
Document retention and deletion rules.
Confirm deployment region before use.
Keep audit logs of handoffs.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
